# CLI reference

This page is the built-in help of the `ticoraw` command-line tool, copied word for word.
You can print the same text yourself with `ticoraw --help` and `ticoraw <command> --help`
(or `ticoraw help <command>`).

For worked examples, see [Converting photos](../converting.md). To install the tool, see
[Install ticoraw](../photographers/install.md).

Commands:

- [`ticoraw convert`](#ticoraw-convert)
- [`ticoraw decode`](#ticoraw-decode)
- [`ticoraw inspect`](#ticoraw-inspect)
- [`ticoraw verify`](#ticoraw-verify)
- [`ticoraw scan`](#ticoraw-scan)
- [`ticoraw report`](#ticoraw-report)

## `ticoraw`

```text
ticoraw: convert Nikon High Efficiency (HE/HE*) NEF raw files to DNG

Usage: ticoraw <command> [options]

Commands:
  convert   Convert HE/HE* NEFs (files or whole directories) to complete DNGs
  decode    Decode one NEF to a complete DNG (or a 16-bit PGM)
  inspect   Describe NEF containers and TicoRAW codestreams without decoding
  verify    Compare a decoded NEF sample-for-sample against a reference DNG
  scan      Classify every NEF in a directory, optionally decoding them all
  report    Print a privacy-safe JSON bug report for one NEF
  help      Show help for a command

Options:
  -h, --help     Show this help (or `ticoraw <command> --help`)
  -V, --version  Show the version

Exit status: 0 on success, 1 on failure, 2 on usage errors.
```

## `ticoraw convert`

```text
Convert High Efficiency (HE/HE*) NEFs to complete DNGs

Usage: ticoraw convert [options] <file|dir>...

Converts every HE/HE* NEF given, or found as a .nef/.nrw file (any case) in a given
directory, to a DNG that keeps the camera's EXIF, GPS, XMP and MakerNote, with the mosaic
in lossless JPEG tiles, a preview, and the NEF's file name as OriginalRawFileName. Classic
(not High Efficiency) NEFs are skipped: editors already support them. Inputs are only read.

Each DNG is written next to its NEF, or with --output under that directory; files found in a
given directory keep their path relative to it there. DNGs are written atomically (a
temporary file, then a rename) and an existing file is never replaced without --force.

Options:
  -o, --output <dir>  Write the DNGs under <dir>, which is created if needed
  -r, --recursive     Descend into subdirectories (symbolic links to directories are skipped)
  --skip-existing     Skip a NEF whose DNG already exists
  -f, --force         Replace existing DNGs
  --uncompressed      Store the mosaic uncompressed (about three times larger)
  --no-preview        Leave out the embedded preview (the thumbnail stays)
  --with-sidecar      Use the sidecar <name>.xmp (any case) next to each NEF, as written by
                      Lightroom, Bridge or Capture One, as the DNG's XMP instead of the
                      NEF's own packet
  -j, --jobs <n>      Files converted at once [default: up to 4, at most one per 2 GB of
                      memory; each file already uses every core]
  --json              Print JSON Lines (one event per file, then a summary) instead of text
  -h, --help          Show this help

On a terminal, a progress line is shown on stderr.

Exit status: 0 when no file failed (skipped files are not failures), 1 when any file
failed, 2 on usage errors.
```

## `ticoraw decode`

```text
Decode one NEF to a complete DNG (or a 16-bit PGM)

Usage: ticoraw decode [options] <file.nef>

Decodes the High Efficiency (TicoRAW) raw strip and writes a complete DNG: the CFA mosaic as
lossless JPEG tiles, the camera's EXIF, GPS, XMP and MakerNote, a preview and a thumbnail,
the colour matrix, as-shot white balance, orientation and default crop, and the input's
file name as OriginalRawFileName. A PGM is the bare mosaic as big-endian 16-bit samples
(maxval 16383 for 14-bit data, else 65535). Output is written atomically and never
overwrites the input. To convert many files, use `ticoraw convert`.

Options:
  -o, --output <path>    Output file [default: the input path with a .dng/.pgm extension]
  --format <dng|pgm>     Output format [default: dng]
  --uncompressed         Store the DNG's mosaic uncompressed (about three times larger)
  --no-preview           Leave out the DNG's embedded preview (the thumbnail stays)
  -f, --force            Overwrite an existing output file
  -h, --help             Show this help

Exit status: 0 on success, 1 on failure, 2 on usage errors.
```

## `ticoraw inspect`

```text
Describe NEF containers and TicoRAW codestreams without decoding pixels

Usage: ticoraw inspect [options] <file.nef>...

Prints the camera model, raw dimensions, codec (TicoRAW HE/HE* or classic Nikon), the
MakerNote compression mode, the raw strip location, black levels and, for TicoRAW strips,
the JPEG XS codestream layout and output transfer curve.

Options:
  --json       Emit a JSON array with one object per file
  -h, --help   Show this help

Exit status: 0 when every file was inspected, 1 if any failed, 2 on usage errors.
```

## `ticoraw verify`

```text
Compare a decoded NEF sample-for-sample against a reference DNG

Usage: ticoraw verify [options] <file.nef> <reference.dng>

Decodes the NEF and the reference DNG's full-resolution CFA image (lossless JPEG or
uncompressed) and compares every sample. Prints the mismatch count, the largest absolute
difference and mismatches per 2x2 CFA site.

Options:
  -h, --help   Show this help

Exit status: 0 only when the images are bit-exact, 1 otherwise, 2 on usage errors.
```

## `ticoraw scan`

```text
Classify every NEF in a directory, optionally decoding them all

Usage: ticoraw scan [options] <dir>

Lists each .nef/.nrw file (any case) as TicoRAW (HE/HE*), classic Nikon, or error, then prints counts.
Files are only read, never modified.

Options:
  --decode         Decode every TicoRAW file; report failures and throughput
  -r, --recursive  Descend into subdirectories (symbolic links to directories are skipped)
  -h, --help       Show this help

Exit status: 0 when every file was classified (and decoded), 1 otherwise, 2 on usage errors.
```

## `ticoraw report`

```text
Print a privacy-safe JSON bug report for one NEF

Usage: ticoraw report <file.nef>

Collects what a bug report about a file needs: the ticoraw version, operating system and
architecture, the camera's make, model and firmware, the Nikon compression mode, the raw
dimensions and codec, the codestream's main header (CAP, PIH, CDT and WGT payloads in hex),
why a codestream is unsupported, and the decode outcome (its time, or the error and the
failing slice).

Nothing personal is included: no serial numbers, GPS position, lens serial, owner, artist or
copyright, no dates, no file name or path, and no pixels. Paste the output into the
bug-report form.

Options:
  -h, --help   Show this help

Exit status: 0 when the report was printed (also when decoding failed), 1 when the file
cannot be read, 2 on usage errors.
```
